create.name: Cedar Rapids Zen Center
create.bio:
Cedar Rapids Zen Center is a small Soto Zen community in Cedar Rapids, Iowa, practising in a house on Bever Avenue in a residential neighbourhood, where a modest zendo can open into the dining room when more people come. It was founded in January 2000, and for nearly twenty-five years its resident teacher was Zuiko Redding, a Texan who had studied with Tozen Akiyama and Dainin Katagiri before ordaining in Japan in 1992 under Tsugen Narasaki; she died in April 2024. The centre's guiding teacher is now Koji Acquaviva, a priest who spent a decade training at San Francisco Zen Center's residential temples, and lay practice leaders keep the schedule running.

Sunday mornings bring zazen, a Dharma talk or discussion, work practice and tea, in person and on Zoom; on some Sundays the sangha listens to a recording of Zuiko's teaching or joins a talk from a sister temple. Short twenty-minute sittings run midweek, a Monday evening group reads and discusses Dharma texts, and newcomers can attend an introduction to zazen once a month. All-day sittings and three-day silent sesshin with oryoki meals deepen the practice, and the centre runs on donations and a modest membership.

courses.title: Practice Opportunities: Sunday zazen and Dharma talks, sesshin and all-day sittings
courses.description: Sunday mornings of zazen followed by a Dharma talk or discussion, work practice and tea, plus short weekday sittings, Monday evening Dharma study, three-day silent sesshin and less formal all-day sittings. In person and on Zoom.
courses.price: Donations are welcome; there is no fee

courses.title: Introduction to Zazen
courses.description: A monthly beginners' evening on the third Wednesday with a talk on Zen, sitting instruction, a short period of zazen and time for questions, plus guidance on zendo etiquette for first visits.
courses.price: Donations are welcome; there is no fee

courses.title: Membership
courses.description: Membership for those who want to support the centre and take part in its life, with library borrowing and a vote at the annual meeting; a traditional membership given in work or goods is also possible by arrangement.
courses.price: General membership – $30; Student/Limited income/Out of Town membership – $15

free_resources.title: Welcome to Cedar Rapids Zen Center: What is Zen?
free_resources.description: A short introduction to Zen as meeting life as it is, with zazen described as sitting quietly in equanimity and carrying that attention off the cushion into daily life.
